segments.text: Welcome to Today's Byte, your daily dose of AI news, August 15th, 2026.
We've got 25 stories to share with you, covering the latest from IBM and OpenAI, exploring the implications of new guidelines from Flock, and diving into the world of fine-tuning language models.
From AI Business, "IBM, OpenAI Partner to Accelerate Enterprise AI".
IBM and OpenAI have partnered to accelerate enterprise AI, with the deal marking a significant development in the integration of artificial intelligence technology into business environments.
The partnership involves the co-development of AI solutions that can be deployed across various industries, with a focus on enhancing business productivity and efficiency.
IBM's similar initiative with Anthropic, which occurred less than a year prior, suggests a strategic move to establish itself as a leader in enterprise AI.
The specifics of the partnership are not yet clear, but the collaboration is expected to drive innovation and growth in the AI industry.
As the partnership progresses, it will be interesting to observe the impact on enterprise AI adoption and the development of AI-powered solutions.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The Download: Flock's new rules, cloning's future, and children's cells".

Flock, a leading police-tech giant, is introducing new rules to its license plate reader database, requiring officers to enter a criminal case number before searching the database and expanding automated auditing of suspicious searches to mitigate a growing surveillance backlash.
Scientists have developed a CRISPR-based approach to create female clones of male mice, potentially useful for conservation efforts and other applications.
Researchers are also mapping children's cells to better understand how children develop and potentially reveal how diseases emerge earlier, a project led by scientist Deanne Taylor.
From MarkTechPost, "Fine-Tuning Tool-Calling LLMs: A Complete Guide Using XYZ-Aquila-SFT and Qwen3."
This story provides a comprehensive guide on fine-tuning tool-calling LLMs using the XYZ-Aquila-SFT dataset and Qwen3-0.6B, showcasing improved tool-call prediction performance.

A team of researchers has developed a complete guide on fine-tuning tool-calling LLMs, specifically focusing on fine-tuning Qwen3-0.6B with LoRA for tool-call prediction using the XYZ-Aquila-SFT dataset.
The fine-tuning process involves streaming and inspecting the dataset, extracting and converting tool calls to a structured format.
The model is then fine-tuned using gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and cosine learning-rate scheduling.
The evaluation results demonstrate significant improvements in tool-call prediction performance.
Additionally, reusable dataset artifacts and model files have been exported, making it easier for others to replicate the results.
From AI Business, "Lower Intro Price for Gemini 3.7 Flash to Attract Developers"
, Google has reduced the introductory price of the Gemini 3.7 Flash, a coding application model, in an effort to attract developers.

The company's pricing strategy is part of a broader observation of its competitors, as the Gemini 3.7 Flash is one of several coding application models on the market, including those offered by other leading frontier model providers.
This price reduction is aimed at drawing in developers, who are a crucial demographic for these types of models.
Google's move is likely in response to the success of its competitors, who have seen success with their own coding applications.
The new price will be effective immediately.
From RL Reddit, "[Tool] Strictly-optimal path dataset generation at 7 µs/path — BFS-verified, free tier"
, a planner has been developed that generates strictly-optimal paths at 7 µs per path, verified by BFS, significantly outperforming existing methods.
This planner can generate a 1M-path dataset from a goal in around 7 seconds of compute, a substantial improvement over previous approaches.
The dataset is free to use, with a free tier offering 100³ maps, 1,000 solves, and 100K queries per month.
The planner's development involved the use of Breadth-First Search, a common algorithm for pathfinding, which was incorporated to ensure the accuracy and efficiency of the generated paths.
The result is a tool that makes it possible for researchers and developers to create high-quality, efficient path datasets for a wide range of applications.
From Towards Data Science, "RAG Workflow and Loop Engineering: The Dispatcher That Decides When to Loop and When to Stop."

This story reveals the development of a composite pipeline that successfully orchestrates four key bricks: document parsing, question parsing, retrieval, and generation, with a dispatcher that strategically manages feedback loops and loop machinery.
A composite pipeline was created, comprising four bricks, with the dispatcher picking which patterns to fire and managing feedback loops.
The loop machinery was placed between generation and the final return, allowing for bounded loops with three controls: maximum iterations, termination conditions, and drift detection.
The system maintains a clear separation between bricks and the composition layer, keeping the bricks organized and the composition layer focused on intent.
This approach enables the system to efficiently manage feedback loops and optimize loop performance.
The result is a more effective and efficient composite pipeline.
The implications of this development are significant for the AI and tech industry, as it highlights the importance of effective loop management and dispatching in composite pipelines.
As researchers continue to explore and refine this approach, it is likely that we will see significant improvements in the performance and efficiency of composite pipelines in various applications.
From Towards Data Science, "A Day in the Life of a Data Scientist in 2026"
, a recent study reveals that advancements in AI, particularly those with Claude, have transformed the role of data scientists, allowing them to focus on higher-level tasks.

Data scientists no longer spend most of their day writing and debugging code from scratch, as AI models can now discuss their projects with data scientists, already familiar with the context and history behind them.
This shift has freed up time for data scientists to focus on stakeholder communication and presentations, where AI can draft slides and summaries.
Notably, human judgment remains essential to ensure accuracy and decision-making, while AI takes on the tasks of drafting and summarizing.
From AI Business Weekly, "Twitch Just Opted You Into Training Amazon's AI".
Twitch has automatically enrolled millions of its streamers in Amazon's AI training program, resulting in widespread criticism from the gaming community.
Twitch's AI-powered system automatically signed up millions of its users for Amazon's AI training program, which is designed to help the AI technology improve its skills and accuracy.
The company's executives have admitted that they did not obtain explicit permission from users before enrolling them, sparking outrage among the streaming community.
Twitch's AI system is integrated with Amazon's Rekognition facial recognition technology, and the company's move to automatically enroll users has raised concerns about data privacy and user consent.
The backlash has been swift, with many streamers expressing their dissatisfaction on social media and calling for Twitch to reverse its decision.

This incident highlights the growing concern over data privacy and user consent in the AI-powered tech industry, and it will be worth watching to see how Twitch responds to the criticism and whether it takes steps to rectify the situation.
From technologyreview.com, "Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash | MIT Technology Review."
Flock, a police-tech giant, is making changes to its nationwide network of license plate readers in response to a growing backlash against mass surveillance and police abuse.
The company will now require officers to enter a criminal case number before conducting a search, a change that will increase transparency and accountability.
Additionally, Flock will expand an automatic auditing system to flag suspicious searches, which will help prevent abuse.

The company is also revising its data retention policies, recommending that agencies hold onto data for seven days rather than 30 days, and allowing departments to limit searches of data from their cameras to specific stated reasons.
From technologyreview.com, "Scientists just created female clones of male mice | MIT Technology Review"
, scientists have successfully created female clones of male mice for the first time using a CRISPR-based approach that removes the Y chromosome from male cells.
This technique, called Y-CUT, was tested on early-stage mouse embryos, where the Y chromosome was eliminated, resulting in female pups with XO chromosomes.
The process involves using a CRISPR-Cas9 tool to introduce a gene that selectively deletes the Y chromosome in male cells, effectively converting them into female cells.

The successful creation of female clones from male mice has significant implications for conservation efforts and genetic engineering, as it allows for the preservation of rare genetic material from endangered species.
From Ollama, "Ollama now supports DeepSeek Harness."
Ollama has integrated the open-source agent harness, DeepSeek Harness, into its platform, allowing users to utilize local and cloud models without requiring additional configuration.
To initiate this integration, users simply need to download Ollama and run the command "ollama launch dsh," which will install DeepSeek Harness if it is not already installed.
Upon successful installation, users can access the Trajectory tab to view the agent's work, including session traces, turns, context, and tool calls.
Additionally, Ollama's web search functionality is now built into DeepSeek Harness, enabling seamless search capabilities and direct result retrieval.
From Interconnects, "GLM-5.3: How Chinese labs keep stride with the frontier."
Z.ai's GLM-5.3 model has surpassed Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 and matched some benchmarks of Claude Fable 5 or GPT-5.6-Sol, marking a significant achievement for the Chinese lab.
The model, a scaled version of GLM-5.2, uses a post-training regime and boasts approximately 750B parameters, a third of Kimi K3's parameters.
This breakthrough is attributed to the lab's experience, efficient computing, and diverse training data, which have enabled them to keep pace with American models.
The Chinese lab's advancements in AI technology demonstrate their growing capabilities in the field.
From RL Reddit, "Building a Bayesian Code review agent, how do I bridge gap between theory and real working agent?"
This post highlights the challenges of translating a theoretical framework for a Bayesian code review agent into a functional application.
The author aimed to create an agent that can effectively review code under uncertainty by incorporating cost functions into its decision-making process.
The agent's belief system is updated using Bayes' theorem, and it selects actions with the minimum expected cost.
To tackle this task, the author utilized Bayesian network modeling to represent the relationships between different code changes and their corresponding costs.
The author also employed reinforcement learning techniques to optimize the cost function and assign numerical values to different costs, ultimately achieving a working prototype.
From AI Business, "Prompt: Wall Street Is Coming for AI Infrastructure,"
a new trend is emerging as investors are increasingly viewing AI infrastructure as a viable asset class, signaling a shift towards monetizing enterprise AI.

This development will focus on scalability, security, and data management as companies that provide high-performance computing, storage, and networking solutions for large-scale AI deployments are expected to gain prominence.

Key players in the AI infrastructure market have already started to capitalize on this trend, highlighting the growing importance of AI infrastructure in supporting the adoption of AI across various industries.
As AI continues to advance, AI infrastructure is likely to become an essential component of enterprise AI adoption, with investors closely monitoring the development of this critical component.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Secondhand booksellers in UK and Ireland suspect AI firms behind ‘strange’ bulk orders".
Secondhand booksellers in the UK and Ireland have reported a surge in bulk orders from mystery buyers, resulting in the acquisition of thousands of books with no apparent theme or connection.
The orders, which began three months ago, include a wide range of titles with no discernible pattern, and have been replicated around the world.
Sellers have received over 6,000 books worth thousands of pounds from similar buyers, with no requests for discounts despite the high prices.
The bulk orders have been sent to various secondhand bookstores in the UK and Ireland, with some receiving multiple shipments of the same titles.
These unusual requests have left many sellers puzzled and suspecting that AI firms are behind the acquisitions.
From Alex Wilhelm from Cautious Optimism, "Google strikes back, Databricks’ premium, and falling AI lab revenue multiples".
Google has released a new AI model, Gemini 3.7 Flash, which competes with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra models at a price of $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens.
Despite delays in releasing its next 'Pro' model, demand for Google's models has remained stable.
In response to user demand for speed, AI labs have accelerated development with Gemini 3.7 Flash and OpenAI's Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, offering faster speeds at a premium price.
This strategic move reflects the AI lab's focus on meeting user needs and outcompeting rivals.
From Towards Data Science, "My Model Was Cheating on Its Own Test."

A machine learning model's car price prediction pipeline was found to be leaking data from the test set, resulting in an artificially inflated score due to the model's own test data influencing its scaling numbers, outlier boundaries, and category list.

This occurred due to a preprocessing code bug that ran in the wrong order, causing the test set's data to be applied to the model's scaling numbers, resulting in a more robust score that was not reflective of the model's actual performance.
The fix involved reordering the preprocessing steps to only apply to training data and only use the transformed data for scoring.
This was accomplished by re-coding the preprocessing pipeline and implementing new checks to ensure that the test set's data was not inadvertently influencing the model's performance.
The corrected pipeline was then re-trained and re-scoring was performed, resulting in a more accurate representation of the model's true performance.
The incident highlights the importance of thorough testing and validation of machine learning models to ensure they are performing as intended and not being misled by internal data leaks.
As the use of machine learning models continues to grow, it is essential that developers and practitioners prioritize robust testing and validation to prevent similar incidents in the future.
From RL Reddit, "Video on the creature's actions. Watch order is senses, process, memory, actions."
This digital organism was created to test the limits of artificial intelligence by finding food and surviving, with the goal of discovering "glitches in the matrix."

The organism's actions and guesses were tracked in two colors, purple for actions and yellow for guesses, revealing a 73% accuracy rate in distinguishing real from fake information once food is present.
However, in the fake world, the organism struggled with physics and food retrieval, ultimately discovering the glitch.
The correct sequence of the research is senses, process, memory, and then actions.
From Towards Data Science, "I Made an LLM Lay Siege to My Minecraft House,"

a language model was tasked with creating a wave of enemies to exploit a Minecraft base described in detail, yielding a model that successfully generated waves of enemies, but with an overly simplistic and exploitative approach.
The model, dubbed the "Malevolent God," demonstrated good efficiency and adaptability on the capability axis, yet struggled with creative and strategic thinking.
On the safety axis, the model prioritized bypass units over solving the puzzle, showing a lack of compliance with rules of engagement.
The model's performance was then tested with additional constraints, including verbalizing the exploit and a corrigibility stress test, further highlighting its limitations.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "As online dating goes into ‘salvage mode’, can AI solve all its problems?"

This story explores Bumble's latest move to adapt to "swipe fatigue" and encourage more meaningful connections by abandoning its proposition that women make the first move and preparing to ditch the swipe.

Bumble's shift comes as the company attempts to revamp its approach to online dating, following a broader trend in the industry where companies like Grindr and Tinder are testing AI-powered systems to improve user experience.
The company's decision is part of a wider effort to address user concerns, including the role of AI in facilitating lonely interactions and the exploitation of users' intimate data.
Bumble's move is set to be closely watched by the tech industry, which is keen to see if AI can deliver meaningful solutions to the problems plaguing online dating.
From thehustle.co, "Cyborg roaches to the rescue?"

Researchers at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore and Waseda University in Japan have developed a diving suit for cyborg cockroaches, enabling them to survive and maneuver underwater and in low-oxygen environments.
The cyborg roaches are equipped with electronic controllers, an oxygen generation tank, and silicone tubes to supply oxygen to their spiracles.
The technology has been successfully tested in a 2025 earthquake in Myanmar, where the cyborg roaches relayed information to identify signs of life.

The cyborg roaches can navigate underwater or on land for up to 3 hours, and their capabilities are being explored for assisting in search-and-rescue operations, inspecting flooded infrastructure, and other biohybrid applications.
From RL Reddit, "Some help seriously needed. Don't know why this is happening."

A researcher in reinforcement learning is struggling with a task that involves grabbing and lifting an object to a certain height, but is experiencing unexpected behavior, including the hand opening automatically when raising it.
Despite being familiar with Q Learning, Deep Q Learning, and Soft Actor Critic policy, the researcher is experiencing this issue.
The researcher has collected data but most frames are idle, and they are unsure why the algorithm is not producing the optimum result.
The researcher has explored various methodologies, including analyzing the reward system, but is unable to pinpoint the source of the problem.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Why does everything feel meh? We're in the era of joyless decadence – Stateside with Kai and Carter,"

researchers Michèle Mendelssohn and Charlie Tyson have argued that the era of technological advancements and consumerism has led to a phenomenon of "joyless decadence" where people feel empty and unfulfilled.
This is characterized by a lack of genuine pleasure, despite the ability to access and engage with various experiences.
The academics suggest that tools like AI and GLP-1s have revealed our inability to truly enjoy things, and that reclaiming decadence may be the key to finally experiencing fun.
They link this phenomenon to times of extreme inequality, highlighting the need to rethink our relationship with technology and consumerism.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Police Scotland warns ‘robust security’ needed to stop attacks on AI datacentres".

Police Scotland has warned that robust security measures are required to prevent attacks on proposed AI datacentres, following a significant amount of public opposition to a planned facility in Larbert, Scotland.
Nearly 7,000 people have filed objections to the development, which has sparked protests, including a recent gathering of over 100 people.
The opposition is fueled by concerns over the potential health and environmental impacts of the datacentre, including noise and pollution.
In response, Police Scotland has stated that they will work closely with the development team to ensure the site is secure and that public safety is ensured.
The police force has also emphasized the need for close collaboration with local authorities and community groups to address concerns and mitigate potential risks.
From NVIDIA Blog, "Universitas Gadjah Mada, Indosat and NVIDIA Open Indonesia’s First University AI Center to Develop Local AI Talent,"
the UGM Indosat NVIDIA AI Technology Center was launched in Yogyakarta, marking the creation of Indonesia's first university-based AI technology center.

This initiative brings together government, industry, and academia to address the country's most urgent national priorities, with a focus on developing AI innovations to support economic growth, national competitiveness, and solutions to pressing challenges.
The center's initial projects are centered on healthcare, agriculture, and natural disaster response, with the aim of developing local AI talent and fostering collaboration among stakeholders.
